title: Vectors in Three Dimensions
seo_title: Year 13 A Level Maths: 3D Vectors Worksheets
standard_text: Use vectors in two dimensions and in three dimensions; calculate the magnitude and direction of a vector; add vectors and multiply by scalars; understand and use position vectors and the distance between two points.
meta_desc: Free Year 13 A level maths worksheets on 3D vectors: distance between points, unit vectors, parallel vectors, midpoints and position vectors. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: A unit vector has magnitude 1: divide by the magnitude.
body_html:
How it works

Distance between (x₁, y₁, z₁) and (x₂, y₂, z₂) is √((x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)² + (z₂ − z₁)²). Parallel vectors are scalar multiples of each other.

Example

Distance from (1, 2, 3) to (3, 5, 9).

√(4 + 9 + 36)

Answer: 7

Common mistakes

  • Forgetting the z-component.
  • Subtracting position vectors the wrong way round.
  • Not dividing by the magnitude for a unit vector.

faq.q: How do you find the distance between two points in 3D?
faq.a: Subtract the coordinates, square each difference, add them and take the square root.

faq.q: How do you find a unit vector?
faq.a: Divide the vector by its magnitude.
